prompt:
An electric car travels at a steady speed of 20 m s^-1 along a straight, horizontal road. The total resistive force opposing the motion (air drag and tyre rolling resistance) is 650 N. The overall efficiency of the car's electric motor and transmission system is 78% (0.78).
(a) Calculate the useful mechanical power output required to maintain this speed. [2]
(b) Calculate the electrical power input supplied by the car battery. [1]
(c) Calculate the energy dissipated as heat in the motor and transmission during a 15 minute journey at this speed. [1]
hints: In (a), at constant speed driving force equals resistive force. Use P = Fv.
In (c), calculate wasted power and multiply by time in seconds (15 min = 900 s).
solution:
(a) Since speed is constant, driving force F = resistive force = 650 N. Useful mechanical power P_useful = Fv = 650 N * 20 m s^-1 = 13 000 W = 13 kW.
(b) Electrical input power P_in = P_useful / eta = 13 000 W / 0.78 = 16 667 W approx 17 kW (or 16.7 kW).
(c) Wasted power P_wasted = P_in - P_useful = 16 667 W - 13 000 W = 3667 W. Time t = 15 * 60 s = 900 s. Energy dissipated E_wasted = P_wasted * t = 3667 W * 900 s = 3.30 * 10^6 J = 3.3 MJ.
teacher_walkthrough: Step (a) links Newton's first law (balanced forces at constant speed) with mechanical power P = Fv.
Step (b) applies the power formulation of efficiency.
Step (c) requires conversion of minutes to seconds: 15 min = 900 s.
